subject: chopperMotorbike
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: custom chopper motorbike.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm planning a stylized Overwatch-style chopper motorbike as a single TS module, with bold chunky shapes and glowing accents, keeping it mostly static geometry but possibly adding wheel joints for a bit of articulation.

I'm figuring out the overall proportions of the bike and constructing the front and rear wheels using scaled torus shapes for fat tires, positioning them so they sit correctly on the ground, then moving on to build rims with glowing neon rings, a hub, and spokes.

For color and style, I'm settling on an Overwatch-inspired palette: deep navy or charcoal body with orange accents, plus cyan glowing energy rings on the wheels, along with a custom hexagonal emblem decal rather than copying the actual logo. Now I'm starting to lay out the main structural parts like the engine block.

Going part by part now: a V-twin engine with angled cylinders, finned heads, and chrome exhaust pipes with glowing tips; a tubular steel frame; a teardrop gas tank painted with orange-charcoal stripes and the emblem; a leather seat with stitching detail; a swept rear fender; raked front forks with a triple tree, glowing headlight, ape-hanger handlebars, grips, and mirrors; and a rear swingarm with coil shocks, all set at roughly a 35° steering rake.

I'm working out the exact geometry for the extended chopper fork -- calculating the angle between the steering head and front axle positions so the rake looks dramatic but still visually balanced, aiming for something close to 45 degrees from vertical.

Now I'm placing the remaining components: headlight nestled near the fork, handlebars up top, the fuel tank and seat positions along the backbone frame, and the engine centered low between the wheels so it sits above the ground clearance line, with the rear wheel set back to establish the overall wheelbase.

I'm also sketching the fender as a curved sweep arcing over the rear wheel, planning symmetric exhaust pipes running back from the cylinders with a glowing tip, and working out the swingarm pivot points connecting to the rear wheel.

Now I'm adding glowing accents: a cyan torus ring inside the wheel, headlight and taillight lenses, orange exhaust tips, and a glowing cyan reactor cylinder nestled between the engine cylinders for a techy look. I'm also considering decals for the tank, like an emblem and stripe texture.

I'm planning to borrow chrome metal and glow materials from the clockwork kit, while using my own SVG dial for the speedometer, and designing a custom cel-shaded paint for the tank body with orange on top and charcoal below with a stripe.

I'm adding mechanical details — forward foot pegs, brake discs, a chain running from the engine sprocket to the rear hub, and coil-spring rear shocks — then setting up a reusable wheel helper function that takes center position, radius, tube radius, width, and spoke count as parameters.

Generating spoke geometry...

Building the fork geometry next, with mirrored sleeves on each side running from the triple tree down to the axle, plus a steering head tube positioned slightly offset from the fork lines to connect the frame's front end properly.

Now I'm working out the handlebars, using a chrome riser sweep curving up and back from the triple tree to ape-hanger grips with darker grip ends near the tips.

Next I'm positioning the headlight assembly, placing a scaled sphere with a torus bezel between the fork tubes, and adding an inner glowing lens cylinder tinted cream-yellow against an orange outer bezel.

For the tank I'm shaping a scaled sphere positioned above the backbone with a chrome cap on top, making sure it clears the frame below. Then I'm defining the seat as a loft through three stations tapering from front to back, painted a dark slate color to contrast with the bike's trim.

Now I'm planning a sissy bar made of chrome rods sweeping up from the rear frame with a curved top, plus an orange rear fender with a glowing red taillight. I'm working out the angular positions around the wheel's radius to place the fender points from front to back.

Next I'm building the engine: a metal crankcase box near the center, with front and rear V-twin cylinders angled in the YZ plane, each with stacked cooling fin discs along their axis.

I'll raise the tank center higher so it clears the backbone, with the seat positioned behind it sloping down. For the engine, I'm adding a small glowing cyan cylinder badge between the V of the cylinders to suggest a primary cover accent, then moving on to plan the exhaust pipes.

Plotting the exhaust path on both sides, sweeping from the cylinder heads back past the swingarm and clear of the rear tire, ending with a glowing orange tip ring beside the wheel using a chrome-radius sweep with flat caps.

I'm placing forward footpegs with angled support rods from the engine, then starting on the front brake disc geometry, working out hub position relative to the fork axle and tire width.

Now I'm positioning the rear axle, sprocket, and swingarm offsets, then sketching the chain as a pair of parallel belt rods connecting the engine sprocket to the rear sprocket.

I'm also placing the rear shocks as coil springs angled from swingarm to frame, and setting up the rear subframe rails and seat triangle struts.

I still need the lower cradle frame tubes down to the engine mounts, a chrome air cleaner cylinder beside the engine, and the emblem details for the fuel tank badge.

Now I'm placing the tank decals on each side using the emblem texture, then adding a speedometer gauge on the triple tree with a circular dial plane angled back toward the rider.

Adding glowing dial details and extra fairing panels...

Working out the fender sweep geometry, I'm computing coordinates at several angles to make sure the fender arcs clear the fork and wrap properly around the front wheel.

Now I'm planning the actual sweep code, using a tapered box section along a catmull-spline path to build the fender shape, with flat caps and verifying the color count stays well under budget.

I'm setting up color constants for the paint job—orange, navy, charcoal, cream, cyan, red—and defining a paint function for the tank that masks by vertical position for a two-tone look.

Now I'm building a wheel helper function, adding a tire torus positioned and scaled by the given parameters, with treads shaped by torus geometry segments.

Still finalizing scene code...
